blocks.content: The superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to the Panchayats shall be vested in a State Election Commission.

Same as a High Court Judge

items: Elections to State Legislative Assemblies are conducted by the Election Commission of India (ECI), NOT the State Election Commission (SEC).
Although appointed by the Governor, the State Election Commissioner can be removed only in the manner prescribed for a High Court Judge.
SEC is an independent constitutional authority and is NOT subordinate to or controlled by the Election Commission of India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The State Election Commission is an autonomous constitutional body created under Article 243K (Panchayats) and Article 243ZA (Municipalities).
The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor of the state.
The conditions of service and tenure of office of the State Election Commissioner are determined by the Governor.
The State Election Commissioner can be removed from office only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of a High Court.
State Election Commissions operate independently and are not subordinate to the Election Commission of India.
